title: A misconception code the list lacks
statement: Whether a wrong option grounded in the text may carry a misconception code the governing list does not name, or must be remapped to the nearest listed one, is unsettled.
example: One audit found a lesson's governing standard pinning exactly four misconception codes while a wrong option grounded in the passage carried a fifth.
detail: An audit of a Grade 5 reading lesson found a wrong option coded to a misconception id outside the four ids its governing bar pins, although the option, a confusion about population size, was correctly grounded in the passage. The audit left the choice to be confirmed against the governing curriculum: allow a fifth id, or remap the option to the nearest pinned one. The shipped content file still carries the invented code.
against: Another learning takes each item's wrong options from the misconceptions recorded for its knowledge statement, which leans toward remapping.

evidence.quote: G5-BAR §7 pins exactly four `feedback_map` ids; this one isn't among them even though the content it's attached to (line 420, population-size confusion) is correctly grounded in the passage. Suggested fix: confirm with canon whether a fifth id is permitted, or remap to the nearest pinned id.
